words.ex: The diamond showed a tiny sparkle in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 钻石在阳光下显示出一丝闪光。
words.en: If something sparkles, it shines brightly with a lot of small points of light.

words.tr:
n. 皱纹
v. 起皱纹；弄皱…
words.ex: He has a deep wrinkle on his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他的额头上有一道深深的皱纹。
words.en: A wrinkle is a small line or fold in something, especially fabric or the skin.

words.ex: She walked with grace across the stage.
words.ex_cn: 她优雅地走过舞台。
words.en: Grace is the quality of being pleasant, polite, and dignified, or a period of time allowed for something to be done.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.ex: Her smile has a special charm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑有一种特别的魅力。
words.en: If you say that someone has charm, you mean that they behave in a friendly and pleasant way that makes people like them. A charm is also a small ornament that is fixed to a bracelet or necklace.

words.tr:
n. 荣誉；荣幸；尊敬；
v. 尊敬；给予荣誉；履行；
words.ex: He received an honor for his brave actions.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢的行为获得了荣誉。
words.en: Honor is a quality that combines respect, pride, and honesty. A person who has honor is someone who is admired and respected because of his or her integrity and ethical behavior.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: The sun shone with great glory at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分，太阳闪耀着辉煌的光辉。
words.en: High renown or honor won by notable achievements; magnificence or great beauty.

words.ex: She is fond of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢巧克力。
words.en: If you are fond of someone or something, you feel affection for them or like them very much.

words.tr:
n. 喜爱；赞同；
v. 赞成；偏爱；有利于；
words.ex: He has a favour for chocolate ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 他特别喜欢巧克力冰淇淋。
words.en: If you regard something or someone with favour, you like or support them.

words.tr:
n. 风味；味道；
v. 给…添风味；
words.ex: This ice cream has a sweet flavour.
words.ex_cn: 这种冰淇淋有甜美的风味。
words.en: Flavour is the taste of a food or drink, especially when it is pleasant and distinctive.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；有代表性的；
words.ex: This is a typical example of a sunny day.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个晴天的典型例子。
words.en: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.tr:
n. 记号；分数；痕迹；
v. 做标记；（使）留痕迹；评分；
words.ex: He put a mark on the map to show the place.
words.ex_cn: 他在地图上做了一个记号来表示那个地方。
words.en: A mark is a small area or spot on a surface which is different in colour or texture from the area around it. If you mark something, you make a mark on it in order to identify it or to give information about it.

words.ex: He remarked that the weather was nice.
words.ex_cn: 他评论说天气很好。
words.en: If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.

words.tr:
v. 评论；表达意见；
n. 评论；意见；
words.ex: He commented on the movie last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚对这部电影发表了评论。
words.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.ex: The concert was terrific!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something or someone as terrific, you are very pleased with them or very impressed by them.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 壮观的；辉煌的；极好的；
words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was splendid.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落非常壮观。
words.en: If you say that something is splendid, you mean that it is very good.

words.ex: The view from the hill is marvellous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色绝妙极了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as marvellous, you are emphasizing that they are extremely good, enjoyable, or impressive.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.tr:
v. 想知道；
n. 惊奇；奇迹；
words.ex: I wonder why he is late.
words.ex_cn: 我想知道他为什么迟到了。
words.en: To feel curiosity or doubt about something; a feeling of surprise mingled with admiration, caused by something beautiful, unexpected, unfamiliar, or inexplicable.

words.ex: The child's recovery was a miracle.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的康复是个奇迹。
words.en: A miracle is an event that cannot be explained by the laws of nature and is therefore considered to be the work of a divine agency.

words.tr:
n. 魔术；魔法；
adj. 魔术（似）的；神奇的；
words.ex: He performed magic at the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 他在生日聚会上表演了魔术。
words.en: Magic is the power to use supernatural forces to make impossible things happen, such as making people disappear or controlling events in nature.

words.ex: The magnet has a magnetic force.
words.ex_cn: 这块磁铁有磁性。
words.en: If you describe something as magnetic, you mean that it is very attractive to people because it has unusual, powerful, and exciting qualities.

words.ex: The magnet picks up the iron nail.
words.ex_cn: 磁铁吸起了铁钉。
words.en: A magnet is a piece of iron or other material which attracts iron or steel towards it.

words.ex: The parliament passed a new law about education.
words.ex_cn: 国会通过了一项关于教育的新法律。
words.en: A parliament is a legislative body of government, typically composed of elected representatives, that is responsible for making laws and representing the interests of the people.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.ex: The senator speaks to the people every week.
words.ex_cn: 这位参议员每周都对人民讲话。
words.en: A senator is a member of a senate, which is a governing body in many countries, especially in the United States.

words.tr: n. 理事会；委员会；议会；
words.ex: The city council made a new rule about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 市政府理事会制定了关于回收的新规定。
words.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

words.ex: The weather bureau issued a storm warning.
words.ex_cn: 气象局发布了风暴预警。
words.en: A bureau is an office, organization, or government department that collects and distributes information.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.ex: The king governed the land for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 国王统治这个国家50年。
words.en: To govern a country or an organization means to officially control and manage its affairs.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

words.tr:
n. 官员；高级职员；
adj. 官方的；正式的；
words.ex: The official announced new rules for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员宣布了节日的新规定。
words.en: An official is a person who holds a position of authority in a government or organization, or something that is authorized or formally recognized.

words.ex: The officer gave a clear order to the soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 军官向士兵下达了明确的命令。
words.en: An officer is a person in a position of authority in the armed forces, the police, or a government organization.

words.ex: The minister signed the new law.
words.ex_cn: 部长签署了新法律。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department or a member of the clergy in some Christian churches.

words.ex: The ministry of education controls schools.
words.ex_cn: 教育部管理学校。
words.en: A ministry is a government department, especially in Britain, which is responsible for a particular area of administration, such as health or education.

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.tr:
adj. 零下的；负的；
n. 缺点；
prep. 减去；
words.ex: The temperature is minus ten degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 气温是零下十摄氏度。
words.en: A minus is a mathematical symbol that represents subtraction or a negative quantity.

words.tr:
v. 引导；领导；带头；
n. 主导地位；铅；领先；
words.ex: The teacher leads the students to the library.
words.ex_cn: 老师带领学生去图书馆。
words.en: To be in charge of a group, country, or situation; to guide or direct in a course; a position of advantage in a contest or competition; a heavy, malleable, ductile, bluish-white, dense metallic element.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的；一流的；处于领导地位的； v. “lead”的现在分词；带领；领导；
words.ex: He is the leading scientist in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的科学家。
words.en: If something is leading in a particular area, it is the most important or advanced thing in that area.

words.ex: He misleads his friends with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚假的故事误导他的朋友。
words.en: If you say that someone has misled you, you mean that they have made you believe something which is not true, either by telling you a lie or by giving you a wrong idea or impression.

words.ex: He misunderstands the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了这些说明。
words.en: If you misunderstand someone or something, you do not understand them properly.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.ex: He believed his fate was to become a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名教师。
words.en: Fate is a power that is believed to control what happens in the future.

words.tr:
n. 导游；指南；向导；
v. 指导；指引；
words.ex: The guide showed us the ancient temple.
words.ex_cn: 导游带我们参观了这座古庙。
words.en: A guide is someone who shows other people the way to a place in a difficult or unknown region. A guide is also a book that gives you information or instructions to help you do or understand something.

words.ex: Follow the guideline to complete the form.
words.ex_cn: 按照指导路线完成表格。
words.en: A guideline is a set of rules or instructions that are given by an official organization telling you how to do something, especially something difficult.

words.ex: He used a compass to find north.
words.ex_cn: 他用指南针找北方。
words.en: A compass is an instrument that you use for finding directions. It has a dial and a magnetic needle that always points to the north.

words.tr:
v. 计算；看作；清点；
n. 计数；计算；
words.ex: He counts the apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他计算桌子上的苹果数量。
words.en: To determine the total number of a collection of items.

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.tr: n. 优惠券；息票；配给券
words.ex: He used a coupon to buy milk at half price.
words.ex_cn: 他用一张优惠券以半价买了牛奶。
words.en: A coupon is a piece of printed paper that allows you to pay less money than usual for a product, or to get it free.

words.ex: He made the payment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在线支付了。
words.en: A payment is an amount of money that is paid to someone, or the act of paying this money.

words.ex: He will repay the loan next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月会偿还贷款。
words.en: If you repay a loan or a debt, you pay back the money that you owe to the person who you borrowed or took it from.

words.ex: I paid the electric bill yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天付了电费账单。
words.en: A bill is a statement of money owed for goods or services, a proposed law presented to a legislature for approval, a piece of paper money, or the beak of a bird.

words.ex: The bank gave a loan to the student.
words.ex_cn: 银行向学生提供了一笔贷款。
words.en: A loan is a sum of money that you borrow.

words.ex: He paid off his debt last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月还清了债务。
words.en: A debt is a sum of money that you owe someone.

words.ex: The children play on the lawn after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草坪上玩耍。
words.en: A lawn is an area of grass that is kept cut short and is usually part of someone's garden or yard, or part of a park.

words.ex: The cat hid behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 猫躲到了灌木丛后面。
words.en: A bush is a plant which is much smaller than a tree and has a lot of branches.

words.tr:
n. 刷子；灌木丛；
v. 刷；
words.ex: He cleaned the floor with a brush.
words.ex_cn: 他用刷子打扫了地板。
words.en: A brush is an object with a handle and a large number of bristles, hairs, or wires fixed to it, used for cleaning, painting, or arranging hair.

words.ex: He flushes the toilet after using it.
words.ex_cn: 他用完厕所后冲水。
words.en: If you flush, your face goes red because you are hot or ill, or because you are feeling a strong emotion such as embarrassment or anger. To flush a toilet means to cause water to pass through it in order to clean it.

words.tr: n. 引人注目的人或物；溅污的斑点；
words.ex: The new singer became a splash on the music scene.
words.ex_cn: 这位新歌手成为了音乐界引人注目的人物。
words.en: To cause (a liquid) to scatter in drops or small quantities, especially by striking or moving suddenly; to move or strike so as to cause a liquid to scatter in this way.

words.ex: The lion lives in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 狮子生活在丛林中。
words.en: A jungle is a dense, tropical forest that is home to a wide variety of plants and animals.

words.tr:
n. 杂草；野草；
v. 除草；铲除；
words.ex: The garden is full of weeds.
words.ex_cn: 花园里长满了杂草。
words.en: A weed is a wild plant that grows in gardens or fields of crops and is not wanted because it harms the plants that are being grown.

words.ex: The horse eats hay every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马每天早上吃干草。
words.en: Hay is grass which has been cut and dried so that it can be used to feed animals.

words.tr:
n. 领域；田地；场地；运动场；
v. 处理，应付（问题、电话等）；
words.ex: He works in the field of computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机科学领域工作。
words.en: A field is an area of land that is used for a particular purpose, such as growing crops or playing sports.

words.tr:
v. 领会；抓紧；
n. 领会；
words.ex: I couldn't grasp the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 我没能领会这首诗的含义。
words.en: To grasp something means to take it in your hand and hold it firmly.

words.ex: He grabbed the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速抓住了球。
words.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

words.tr:
prep. 在…上面；
adj. 上述的；
adv. 在上面；
words.ex: The book is above the table.
words.ex_cn: 书在桌子上面。
words.en: In or to a higher place than something else; over.

words.ex: The book fell to the bottom of the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书掉到了架子的底部。
words.en: The lowest part or edge of something, especially the part on which it rests or is supported.

words.ex: She sewed a button on her coat.
words.ex_cn: 她把一颗纽扣缝在了外套上。
words.en: A button is a small, usually round object that you press to operate a device or a machine, or a small, round object that you fasten to clothing to keep it closed.

words.ex: The cat is beneath the table.
words.ex_cn: 猫在桌子下面。
words.en: In or to a lower position than someone or something, under someone or something.

words.ex: The cat is underneath the table.
words.ex_cn: 猫在桌子下面。
words.en: If one thing is underneath another, it is directly under it, often so that it is hidden by it.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.tr:
n. 经验；阅历；
v. 经历；体验；
words.ex: He has a lot of experience in teaching English.
words.ex_cn: 他有丰富的英语教学经验。
words.en: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity that you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.tr: n. 一段时间；会议；会期；开庭；学年；
words.ex: We had a long session of studying together.
words.ex_cn: 我们一起学习了一段时间。
words.en: A session is a meeting of a court, parliament, or other official group, or a period of time used for a particular activity, especially by a group of people.

words.tr:
n. 时距；跨度；
v. 跨越；
words.ex: The span of his career was 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的时距是40年。
words.en: The extent or measure of space between two points or extremities, as of a bridge or a roof; the full extent, stretch, or reach of anything.

words.ex: He suffered from a bad cold last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周患了重感冒。
words.en: To experience something unpleasant, such as injury, pain, or loss.

words.ex: He grew a thick beard last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天他留了一脸浓密的胡须。
words.en: The hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.ex: He didn't refer to the book during the talk.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中没有提到那本书。
words.en: If you refer to a particular subject or person, you talk about them or mention them. If you refer to someone or something as a particular thing, you use a particular word, expression, or name to mention or describe them.

words.tr:
n. 担忧；关注；
v. 涉及；
words.ex: His main concern is his child's safety.
words.ex_cn: 他主要的担忧是孩子的安全。
words.en: If something concerns you, it worries you or causes you to feel anxious.

words.ex: The global climate conference was held in Paris.
words.ex_cn: 全球气候大会在巴黎举行。
words.en: A conference is a meeting of people who share the same interests or profession.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.tr: v. 较喜欢；更喜欢；宁愿；
words.ex: I prefer tea to coffee.
words.ex_cn: 我更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: If you prefer someone or something, you like that person or thing better than another, and so you are more likely to choose them if there is a choice.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.ex: The city's skyline looks beautiful at night.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的天际线在夜晚看起来很美。
words.en: The outline of land and buildings defined against the sky.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；纲要；
v. 描画轮廓；概述；
words.ex: The artist drew the outline of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家画出了山的轮廓。
words.en: An outline is a line that shows or forms the outer edge of something, or a general description or plan showing the essential features of something but not the detail.

words.tr:
adv. 在网上地；在线地；
adj. 联机的；在线的；
words.ex: He works online from home.
words.ex_cn: 他在家网上工作。
words.en: Connected to or available through a computer network, especially the Internet.

words.ex: The teacher underlined the key point.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了这个关键点。
words.en: To draw a line under a word or phrase, especially in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: The newspaper's headline said 'City Wins Championship'.
words.ex_cn: 报纸的大字标题写着‘城市赢得冠军’。
words.en: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.

words.ex: He finished his homework before the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 他在截止日期前完成了作业。
words.en: A deadline is a time or date before which a particular task must be finished or a particular thing must be done.

words.ex: The layout of the room makes it feel bigger.
words.ex_cn: 房间的布局让它显得更大。
words.en: The way in which the parts of something are arranged or laid out.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: Parents often spoil their children with too many toys.
words.ex_cn: 父母经常用太多玩具宠坏孩子。
words.en: To spoil something means to reduce its quality or value, often by damaging it in some way. It can also mean to treat someone, especially a child, with too much kindness or indulgence, leading to their detriment.

words.ex: The water begins to boil at 100 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 水在100度时开始沸腾。
words.en: When a liquid boils or when you boil it, it reaches the temperature at which it starts to turn into a gas.

words.tr:
n. 废墟；
v. 破坏；
words.ex: The old temple is now a ruin.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙现在已成为废墟。
words.en: Ruin means the physical destruction or disintegration of something or the state of disintegrating or being destroyed.

words.ex: The storm destroyed the old bridge.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了那座旧桥。
words.en: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.ex: He lived in Paris for a decade.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎生活了十年。
words.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.ex: The outbreak of the flu surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 流感的爆发让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An outbreak of something unpleasant, such as violence or a disease, is a sudden occurrence of it.

words.ex: The scientist made a breakthrough in cancer research.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家在癌症研究中取得了突破。
words.en: A breakthrough is a significant development or achievement that helps to solve a problem or improve a situation.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: His outlook on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的观点非常积极。
words.en: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.

words.ex: The factory's output increased last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂上个月的产量增加了。
words.en: The amount of something produced by a person, machine, or industry.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.tr:
adv. 在夜里；突然；
adj. 整晚的；
words.ex: The baby slept overnight in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿整夜睡在小床上。
words.en: If something happens overnight, it happens during the night or for the period of one night. It can also mean happening very quickly or suddenly.

words.ex: He will overtake the car ahead soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会超过前面的车。
words.en: If you overtake someone, you go past them because you are moving faster than they are.

words.ex: He worked overtime to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他加班完成了这个项目。
words.en: Overtime refers to the time worked beyond one's regular working hours, often with additional pay.

words.ex: The book is overdue at the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆逾期了。
words.en: If you say that a change or an event is overdue, you mean that you think it should have happened before now.

words.ex: He overheard them talking about the party.
words.ex_cn: 他无意中听到他们在谈论派对。
words.en: To overhear is to hear what someone is saying without them knowing that you are listening.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: He will undertake a new project next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将从事一个新项目。
words.en: To undertake a task or job means to start doing it and accept responsibility for it.

words.tr:
adj. 总的；全面的；总体的；
adv. 总计；大致上；
words.ex: The overall cost is too high.
words.ex_cn: 总成本太高了。
words.en: You use overall to indicate that you are talking about a situation in general or about the whole of something.

words.ex: There are altogether five apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上面总共有五个苹果。
words.en: Altogether is used to emphasize that something is completely the case or to indicate the total number or amount of something.

words.ex: People gather in the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们在广场上聚集庆祝节日。
words.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

words.tr: n. 总部；司令部；指挥部；
words.ex: The company's headquarters is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: The main office or center of control of a company, organization, or military unit.

words.tr: n. 四分之一；季度；一刻钟；地区；方向；
words.ex: He ate a quarter of the pizza.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了四分之一的比萨。
words.en: A quarter is one of four equal parts of something, or a period of three months.

words.ex: Please tell me beforehand if you can't come.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不能来，请提前告诉我。
words.en: If you do something beforehand, you do it earlier than a particular event.

words.ex: I am ready for the test.
words.ex_cn: 我准备好考试了。
words.en: If you are ready, you are prepared for something or are in a suitable state to do or deal with it.

words.ex: He is a so-called expert, but he knows little.
words.ex_cn: 他是个所谓的专家，但懂得很少。
words.en: used to show that something or someone is commonly designated by the name or term specified, often to suggest that the name or term is not appropriate or accurate

words.tr:
v. 使腐败；
adj. 腐败的；
words.ex: The official was corrupt by taking bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员因收受贿赂而腐败。
words.en: If someone is corrupt, they do things that are dishonest or illegal in order to gain money or power.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.ex: The company is bankrupt after losing all its money.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司失去所有钱后破产了。
words.en: If a person or a company is bankrupt, they have been declared by a court of law to be unable to pay their debts.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: The camel walks across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼穿越沙漠。
words.en: A desert is a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand. If you desert someone or something, you leave them and no longer help or support them.

words.ex: He ate ice cream for dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他吃冰淇淋当甜食。
words.en: Dessert is a sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.

words.ex: He inserts a coin into the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他把一枚硬币放进机器里。
words.en: To put or introduce something into something else.

words.ex: He dumped the trash into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾倒进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To dump something means to get rid of it quickly and without care, often because it is no longer wanted or needed. It can also refer to the place where waste is left.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.tr: n. 废旧杂物；无价值的东西；
words.ex: He cleaned up the junk in his garage.
words.ex_cn: 他清理了车库里那些废旧杂物。
words.en: Old or discarded articles that are considered useless or of little value.

words.tr: n. 垃圾；无价值的东西；
words.ex: The trash bin is full.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾桶满了。
words.en: Waste material or unwanted things that are thrown away.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.ex: The two teams clashed during the match.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍在比赛中发生了冲突。
words.en: A clash is a loud, harsh noise, like the clash of cymbals. It can also refer to a conflict or disagreement.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.tr:
n. 遇难船只；残骸；
v. 破坏；毁坏；
words.ex: The wreck lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这艘遇难船只沉在海底。
words.en: If something such as a ship or a plane is wrecked, it is damaged so much that it cannot be repaired or it is completely destroyed.

words.ex: He smashed the glass with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃打碎了。
words.en: To break something into pieces violently and noisily, or to cause something to do this by dropping, throwing, or hitting it.

words.ex: He paid with cash for the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他用现金买了面包。
words.en: Money in the form of coins or banknotes, especially that which is immediately available.

words.ex: He felt ashamed for lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对妈妈撒谎而感到羞愧。
words.en: If someone is ashamed, they feel embarrassed or guilty because of something they have done or because of their appearance.

words.ex: Add a dash of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 给汤里加一点盐。
words.en: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly. A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.

words.ex: He sealed the envelope with glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用胶水把信封封上了。
words.en: A seal is a device or substance that is used to close off or fasten an opening or container, making it airtight or watertight. It can also refer to a marine mammal with flippers for swimming.

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: The detective uncovered the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探揭开了真相。
words.en: To uncover something means to remove the cover from it or to reveal it by investigation or inquiry.

words.tr:
n. 负荷；载重；
v. 载入；
words.ex: The bridge can't hold such a heavy load.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥承受不了这么重的负荷。
words.en: A load is a large quantity of something that is carried by a vehicle, person, or animal, or the amount of work that a person or machine has to do.

words.ex: The workers unload the boxes from the truck.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从卡车上卸下箱子。
words.en: To remove goods from a vehicle, ship, container, etc.

words.ex: He unfolded the map on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图在桌子上展开。
words.en: To open or spread out something that is folded; to develop or be revealed.

words.tr:
n. 折痕；褶；
v. 折叠；
words.ex: The paper has a deep fold in the middle.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸中间有一道深深的折痕。
words.en: To bend something, especially paper or cloth, so that one part of it lies flat on top of another part; to be able to be bent in this way.

words.ex: Water is a common substance.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的物质。
words.en: A substance is a particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

words.ex: This is a good instance of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An instance is a particular example or case of something.

words.tr:
v. 引用；报价；
n. 引用；引文；报价；
words.ex: He quoted Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中引用了莎士比亚的话。
words.en: To repeat or copy out (a group of words from a text or speech), typically with an indication that one is not the original author or speaker.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.ex: He withdrew $100 from the ATM.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动取款机里提取了100美元。
words.en: If you withdraw something from a place, you remove it or take it away.

words.ex: He pulled the keys from the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他从抽屉里拿出钥匙。
words.en: A drawer is a sliding container that fits into a piece of furniture, such as a desk or chest, and is used for storing things.

words.ex: Please fetch me a glass of water.
words.ex_cn: 请给我拿一杯水来。
words.en: If you fetch something or someone, you go to the place where they are and return with them.

words.ex: The mountains look distant from here.
words.ex_cn: 从这里看，山显得很远。
words.en: If you describe something as distant, you mean that it is far away in space or time.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.tr:
adj. 立即的；即时的；
n. 瞬间；立即；
words.ex: He wants an instant answer.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一个立即的回答。
words.en: An instant is a very short period of time, or a particular point in time.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.tr: adj. 即刻的；立即的；紧接的；最近的；
words.ex: He needs immediate help.
words.ex_cn: 他需要即刻的帮助。
words.en: An immediate action, event, or situation happens or exists without any delay.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: He will replace the broken chair.
words.ex_cn: 他将代替这把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second.

words.tr:
n. 研究所；学院；协会；
v. 建立；制定；
words.ex: He works at a research institute.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家研究所工作。
words.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. It can also refer to the act of starting something such as a system or an official process.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.tr:
adj. 分开的；分离的；单独的；
v. 分离；隔离；
words.ex: They live in separate houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在分开的房子里。
words.en: To cause to move or be apart; to divide or keep apart.

words.ex: The health sector needs more funding.
words.ex_cn: 医疗部门需要更多资金。
words.en: A particular area of activity, especially one that is part of a larger area of activity or one that is considered separately from other areas.

words.ex: This book has five sections.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有五个部分。
words.en: A section of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: He starts his new class in the fall semester.
words.ex_cn: 他在秋季学期开始他的新课程。
words.en: A semester is one of the two periods that the school or college year is divided into, especially in the United States and Canada.

words.tr:
n. 术语；学期；期限；措辞；
v. 把…称作；把…叫做；
words.ex: The word 'algorithm' is a technical term in computer science.
words.ex_cn: ‘算法’是计算机科学中的一个术语。
words.en: A term is a word or expression used in relation to a particular subject, especially one that has a specific meaning, or a fixed period of time during which something lasts or is intended to happen.

words.ex: The two houses are apart by fifty meters.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子相隔五十米。
words.en: If people or things are apart, they are separated by a distance.

words.tr: n. 单元住宅；公寓住宅；
words.ex: He lives in a small apartment near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他住在公园附近的一间小公寓里。
words.en: An apartment is a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a large building.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.ex: Dust particles float in the air.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘微粒漂浮在空气中。
words.en: A particle is a very small piece or amount of something.

words.ex: He will depart tomorrow morning.
words.ex_cn: 他明天早上离开。
words.en: If you depart from a place, you leave it and start a journey to another place.

words.ex: He only read the partial report.
words.ex_cn: 他只读了部分报告。
words.en: If you describe something as partial, you mean that it is not complete or whole.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: The teacher showed a bias for students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师对早到的学生有偏爱。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: He lives independently and makes his own decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他独立生活，并自己做决定。
words.en: If one thing or person is independent of another, they are separate and not connected, so that the first one is not affected or influenced by the second.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: The gravity of Earth pulls objects down.
words.ex_cn: 地球的重力把物体往下拉。
words.en: Gravity is the force that causes things to fall towards the Earth or towards any other physical body having mass.

words.tr: v. 伤心；悲痛；使悲痛；使伤心
words.ex: He grieves for his lost dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为失去的狗感到悲痛。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or distress, especially because of someone's death.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.ex: His belief in honesty never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对诚实的信念从未改变。
words.en: A belief is a strong feeling that something is true or exists.

words.ex: I believe you are telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 我相信你在说真话。
words.en: If you believe in something, you think that it is true, or that it exists.

words.ex: I am grateful for your help.
words.ex_cn: 我感激你的帮助。
words.en: If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you, you have warm, friendly feelings towards them and wish to thank them.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.ex: He grinds the coffee beans into powder.
words.ex_cn: 他把咖啡豆碾成粉末。
words.en: To reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it.

words.tr:
n. 光泽；上光剂；
v. 擦亮；润色；
words.ex: The polish of the wooden table made it shine.
words.ex_cn: 木桌的光泽让它闪闪发亮。
words.en: If you polish something, you make it smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance. Polish is also a substance that you use to make things smooth and shiny.

words.tr:
v. 爆裂；突然而起；
n. 爆裂；突然而起；
words.ex: The balloon burst when he blew too much air.
words.ex_cn: 当他吹入太多空气时，气球爆裂了。
words.en: If something bursts or if you burst it, it suddenly breaks open or splits open and the air or other substance inside it comes out; used especially to describe the sound of something breaking open.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.tr:
v. 吹；打击；
n. 打击；
words.ex: The wind blows the leaves away.
words.ex_cn: 风吹走了树叶。
words.en: To move air or gas forcefully; to strike something with force.

words.ex: The bomb will explode at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在中午爆炸。
words.en: If an object explodes, it bursts loudly and with great force, often causing damage or injury.

words.ex: They explore the forest to find hidden caves.
words.ex_cn: 他们探索森林以寻找隐藏的洞穴。
words.en: To explore means to travel over or through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it or to search for something valuable.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr:
n. 炸弹
v. 投弹于；轰炸
words.ex: The bomb exploded at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹在中午爆炸了。
words.en: A bomb is a device which explodes and damages or destroys a large area.

words.tr:
v. 撞；碰上；颠簸行进；
n. 碰撞；猛击；肿块；凸块；
words.ex: He bumped the table and spilled his drink.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到了桌子，打翻了饮料。
words.en: If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.

words.ex: They had a bumper harvest this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年他们获得了异常大的收成。
words.en: A bumper is a bar at the front and back of a vehicle that reduces damage if the vehicle hits something.

words.tr:
v. 抽水；打气；
n. 泵；抽水机；打气机；
words.ex: He pumps water from the well every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上从井里抽水。
words.en: A pump is a device that moves fluids (liquids or gases), or sometimes slurries, by mechanical action. Pumps can be classified into three major groups according to the method they use to move the fluid: direct lift, displacement, and gravity pumps.

words.ex: He ate a lump of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块糖。
words.en: A lump is a solid piece of something, often with no particular shape. If you lump things together, you put them together in a group or treat them as the same.

words.tr: v. 射击；拍摄（电影）；疾驰；“shoot”的过去式和过去分词； n. 照片；射击；射门；
words.ex: He shot the target with his gun.
words.ex_cn: 他用枪射击了目标。
words.en: A shot is an act of shooting a gun, or the sound that this makes. It can also refer to an attempt to do something, a photograph, or an injection.

words.tr:
n. 火；
v. 射击；开火；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火在壁炉里熊熊燃烧。
words.en: Fire is the heat and light that comes out when something burns. It can also refer to the act of shooting a weapon or the dismissal of an employee from a job.

words.ex: The company will hire a new manager next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司下周将雇用一位新经理。
words.en: If you hire someone, you employ them or pay them to do a particular job for you.

words.ex: He will retire next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将退休。
words.en: If you retire, you stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age or because you are ill.

words.ex: The company will employ five new workers next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将雇佣五名新员工。
words.en: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

words.ex: He found employment after graduating from university.
words.ex_cn: 他大学毕业后找到了工作。
words.en: the condition of having paid work

words.tr: n. 奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；
words.ex: She bought a luxury dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件奢华的裙子。
words.en: Luxury is very great comfort, especially among beautiful and expensive surroundings.

words.tr:
n. 珍宝；宝物；财富；
v. 珍惜；
words.ex: The old map showed where the treasure was buried.
words.ex_cn: 那张旧地图显示了珍宝埋藏的地方。
words.en: If you treasure something that you have, you keep it or care for it carefully because it gives you great pleasure and you think it is very special.

words.ex: This necklace is precious to her.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链对她来说很珍贵。
words.en: If you say that something such as a resource is precious, you mean that it is valuable and should not be wasted or used badly.

words.ex: Her beloved dog always greeted her at the door.
words.ex_cn: 她钟爱的狗总是在门口迎接她。
words.en: Dearly loved.

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.tr: adj. 有价值的；贵重的；值钱的；
words.ex: This old book is valuable to historians.
words.ex_cn: 这本旧书对历史学家来说很有价值。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as valuable, you mean that they are very useful and helpful.

words.ex: The new phone is too costly for me.
words.ex_cn: 这部新手机对我来说太贵了。
words.en: If you say that something is costly, you mean that it costs a lot of money, often more than you would want to pay.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.tr:
v. 估算；估价；
n. 估价；估算；
words.ex: Can you estimate how long it will take?
words.ex_cn: 你能估算一下需要多长时间吗？
words.en: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

words.ex: I reckon it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我认为明天会下雨。
words.en: If you reckon that something is true, you think that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.tr:
n. 方法；接近；靠近；路径；
v. 接近；靠近；临近；处理；
words.ex: He used a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一种新方法来解决问题。
words.en: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time.

words.ex: He expended all his money on food.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都花在了食物上。
words.en: To expend something, especially energy, time, or money, means to use it or spend it.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr:
n. 首都；财富；大写字母；
adj. 大写的；
words.ex: Beijing is the capital of China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的首都。
words.en: The city or town that functions as the seat of government and administrative center of a country or region.

words.ex: The captain sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船长驾驶船穿越了海洋。
words.en: A captain is the person in charge of a ship or an aircraft, or a leader of a team or group.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr:
v. 记录；准确地描述；俘虏；吸引；
n. 抓捕；
words.ex: The camera can capture the moment clearly.
words.ex_cn: 相机可以清晰地记录下这一瞬间。
words.en: To capture someone or something means to catch them, especially after a chase.

words.ex: The sailors slept in the cabin during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手们在风暴期间睡在船舱里。
words.en: A cabin is a small room or compartment, especially one on a ship or an aircraft.

words.ex: He kept the dishes in the cabinet.
words.ex_cn: 他把盘子放在储藏柜里。
words.en: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves or drawers, used for storing or showing things. In politics, a cabinet is a group of people who are chosen by a head of state to give advice and to help set government policy.

words.ex: The cable connects the computer to the printer.
words.ex_cn: 这条电缆将电脑连接到打印机。
words.en: A cable is a thick wire or rope, or a bundle of wires or ropes, used to carry electricity or electronic signals, or to support a structure.

words.ex: The farmer feeds his cattle every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上喂他的牛。
words.en: Cattle are large domesticated animals that are kept on farms for their milk or meat.

words.ex: He used a thin wire to fix the broken hook.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根细金属丝固定了坏掉的钩子。
words.en: A wire is a long thin piece of metal that is used to fasten things or to carry electric current.

words.ex: This region has many mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区有很多山。
words.en: A region is a large area of land that is different from other areas of land, for example because it is one of the different parts of a country with its own customs and characteristics, or because it has a particular geographical feature.

words.ex: The origin of this tradition is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源不明。
words.en: The origin of something is the point or place where it begins, or the cause from which it arises.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.tr: n. 来源；出处；源泉；源头；提供资料者；
words.ex: The river's source is in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条河的源头在山里。
words.en: The place, person, or thing from which something comes or can be obtained.

words.ex: The school needs more resources for students.
words.ex_cn: 学校需要为学生提供更多的资源。
words.en: A resource is a source or supply from which benefit is produced. Typically resources are materials, energy, services, staff, knowledge, or other assets that are transformed to produce benefit and in the process may be consumed or made unavailable.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.ex: The boy tried to seize the ball.
words.ex_cn: 男孩试图抓住球。
words.en: If you seize something, you take hold of it quickly, firmly, and forcefully.

words.ex: The thieves robbed the bank last night.
words.ex_cn: 小偷昨晚抢劫了银行。
words.en: To rob someone or somewhere means to take money or property illegally from them, often using force.

words.ex: He rubs his hands together to warm them.
words.ex_cn: 他搓手来暖和它们。
words.en: To move one's hand or a cloth repeatedly back and forth on the surface of something with firm pressure.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.ex: He strives to finish his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力完成作业。
words.en: If you strive to do something or strive for something, you make a great effort to do it or get it.

words.ex: He made a big effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他努力完成这个项目，按时交工。
words.en: If you make an effort to do something, you try hard to do it.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.tr:
n. 记录；唱片；
v. 记录；录制；
words.ex: The school keeps a record of all student grades.
words.ex_cn: 学校保存所有学生成绩的记录。
words.en: A record is a piece of information or an account of something that is written down or stored on a computer or other device so that it can be referred to later.

words.ex: The audio signal was clear and loud.
words.ex_cn: 音频信号清晰响亮。
words.en: Audio refers to sound, especially when recorded, transmitted, or reproduced.

words.ex: The audience clapped loudly after the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众热烈鼓掌。
words.en: The group of spectators at a public event; listeners or viewers collectively, especially those attending a performance or reading a particular work.

words.tr:
n. 回声；
v. 回响；
words.ex: The echo came back from the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 回声从山上反弹回来。
words.en: An echo is a sound which is caused by a noise being reflected off a surface such as a wall.

words.tr:
v. 看待；有关；
n. 尊敬；致意；
words.ex: I regard him as a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把他看作好朋友。
words.en: If you regard someone or something as being a particular thing or as having a particular quality, you believe that they are that thing or have that quality.

words.ex: He went outside regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨就出去了。
words.en: If you say that someone does something regardless, you mean that they do it without taking account of the possible problems or difficulties.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.ex: There is a big difference between apples and oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果和橙子之间有很大的差异。
words.en: A difference is a way in which two or more things are not the same.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类凭本能飞向南方。
words.en: An instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

words.tr:
n. 刺；刺痛；
v. 刺；刺痛；
words.ex: The bee gave him a sharp sting.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂给了他一下刺痛。
words.en: If a plant, animal, or insect stings you, it pricks your skin and usually pushes poison into your body with a sharp pointed part of its body.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: The rocket's thrust lifted it into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 火箭的推力将它送上了天空。
words.en: To thrust something somewhere means to push it there quickly and forcefully. A thrust is also a powerful push or movement.

words.ex: The scientist observe the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上观察鸟类。
words.en: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.ex: He deserves a break after working so hard.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作后值得休息一下。
words.en: If you say that a person or thing deserves something, you mean that they should have it or receive it because of their actions or qualities.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.ex: He wears a helmet to protect his head.
words.ex_cn: 他戴头盔来保护头部。
words.en: If you protect someone or something, you prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

words.ex: I can detect a change in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 我能察觉到她情绪的变化。
words.en: To detect something means to find it or discover it, often using special equipment or methods.

words.tr:
n. 侦察兵；
v. 搜寻；
words.ex: The scout watched the enemy's movement quietly.
words.ex_cn: 侦察兵悄悄观察敌人的动向。
words.en: A scout is someone who is sent to an area of countryside to find out the position of an enemy or to search for a suitable place for a military camp.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet can prevent head injuries.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔可以防止头部受伤。
words.en: To prevent something means to stop it from happening or to stop someone from doing something.

words.ex: The school forbids students to use phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: To forbid something means to order that it must not be done.

words.tr:
n. 努力争取；出价；投标；
v. 出价；投标；
words.ex: His bid for the championship inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他为冠军所做的努力鼓舞了所有人。
words.en: To bid means to offer a particular amount of money for something that is being sold, especially at an auction, or to offer to do work or provide services for a particular price.

words.tr:
v. 禁止；
n. 禁止；
words.ex: The school bans phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If there is a ban on something, it is not allowed. If something is banned, it is not allowed to be done, shown, or used.

words.ex: He waved a red banner in the parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在游行中挥舞着一面红旗子。
words.en: A banner is a long strip of cloth with a message or design on it, used especially for advertising or as a symbol of a particular group or cause.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.ex: The museum will exhibit ancient coins next month.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆下个月将展览古钱币。
words.en: To exhibit something means to show it in a public place so that people can go to see it. It can also mean to show a particular quality, ability, or type of behavior.

words.tr:
n. 展示；陈列；
v. 展示；陈列；
words.ex: The store has a big display of new phones.
words.ex_cn: 商店里有一个新手机的展示。
words.en: To display something means to put it in a place where people can see it easily, or to show it to people.

words.tr:
v. （使）结冰；（使）冻结；
n. 严寒期；冻结；
words.ex: The water will freeze in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在寒冷的天气里会结冰。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.ex: He took a deep breath before jumping.
words.ex_cn: 他跳之前深吸了一口气。
words.en: The air taken into or expelled from the lungs.

words.ex: A gentle breeze blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵微风轻轻吹过树梢。
words.en: A breeze is a gentle wind.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.tr:
n. 情节；小块用地；
v. 绘图；
words.ex: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节非常精彩。
words.en: A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, especially against a person or a government. It can also refer to the main events of a play, novel, movie, or similar work, devised and presented by the writer as an interrelated sequence. Additionally, a plot can be a small piece of land that is used or intended for a specific purpose.

words.tr:
n. 公寓；
adj. 平坦的；扁平的；(轮胎)瘪了的；平淡无味的；
adv. 直接地；
words.ex: He lives in a small flat in London.
words.ex_cn: 他住在伦敦的一间小公寓里。
words.en: Something that is flat is level and smooth, with no curved, high, or hollow parts.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The forest is dense with trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林树木茂密。
words.en: Something that is dense contains a lot of things or people in a small area.

words.ex: The steam condenses into water when it touches the cold glass.
words.ex_cn: 当蒸汽接触到冷的玻璃时，会凝结成水。
words.en: If you condense something, especially a piece of writing or a speech, you make it shorter, usually by including only the most important parts.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: The colors of the painting fade in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的颜色在阳光下逐渐消失。
words.en: To gradually grow faint and disappear.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.tr:
n. 影响（力）；
v. 影响；
words.ex: The teacher had a big influence on her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生们有很大的影响。
words.en: The power to affect, control, or manipulate someone or something.

words.ex: He caught influenza last winter.
words.ex_cn: 他去年冬天得了流感。
words.en: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by the influenza virus, characterized by fever, sore throat, muscle pain, severe headache, coughing, and weakness.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: He speaks fluent English.
words.ex_cn: 他讲一口流利的英语。
words.en: If someone is fluent in a particular language, they can speak it easily and correctly.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.tr:
n. 缺乏；短缺；
v. 缺乏；短缺；
words.ex: There is a lack of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.ex: Rare birds can be seen in this forest.
words.ex_cn: 这种森林里可以看到稀有的鸟类。
words.en: Something that is rare is not common and is therefore interesting or valuable.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.tr:
adj. 紧张的；拉紧的；
n. 时态；
words.ex: He felt tense before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到紧张。
words.en: If you are tense, you are anxious and nervous and cannot relax.

words.ex: He took an intensive English course last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他参加了一个密集的英语课程。
words.en: Intensive is used to describe something that involves a lot of effort, energy, or attention in a short period of time.

words.ex: He felt intense pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到剧烈的疼痛。
words.en: If you describe an activity as intense, you mean that it is very serious and concentrated, and often involves doing a great deal in a short time.

words.tr:
n. 意义；感知；理解力；知觉；
v. 感觉到；觉察出；意识到；
words.ex: The story has no sense.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事没有意义。
words.en: A sense is a feeling or awareness about something, or a physical ability such as sight, hearing, touch, taste, or smell.

words.tr: adj. 敏感的；感情脆弱的；体贴的；善解人意的；
words.ex: He is sensitive to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you understand and are aware of them.

words.ex: He talked nonsense and no one understood him.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一些无意义的话，没人能理解他。
words.en: If you say that something spoken or written is nonsense, you mean that you consider it to be untrue or silly.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有判断力的；恰当的；合理的；
words.ex: It is sensible to wear a coat in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 在寒冷的天气里穿外套是明智的。
words.en: A sensible person is able to make good judgments and decisions based on reason rather than emotion.

words.ex: He has a mental illness.
words.ex_cn: 他有心理疾病。
words.en: Relating to the mind or involving the process of thinking.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.tr:
adj. 总的；全部的；
n. 总计；总额；
v. 共计；总数达；
words.ex: The total cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 总费用是50美元。
words.en: The whole amount or number; the sum total.

words.ex: He uses a digital watch to tell time.
words.ex_cn: 他用一块数字手表看时间。
words.en: Digital systems, devices, or technology use electronic signals that are represented by the numbers 1 and 0, indicating 'on' or 'off'.

words.ex: He has a talent for playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他有弹钢琴的才能。
words.en: If someone has a talent for something, they have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: The box contains five apples.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子包含五个苹果。
words.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: The floor is dirty after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后，地板变得肮脏了。
words.en: If something is dirty, it is marked or covered with stains, spots, or mud, and needs to be cleaned.

words.ex: The river is dirty because of pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这条河因为污染而变得肮脏。
words.en: Pollution is the process of making air, water, soil, etc. dirty and not safe or suitable to use.

words.ex: He retains his old photos in a box.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧照片保存在一个盒子里。
words.en: If you retain something, you keep it or continue to have it.

words.tr: v. 保持；维护；坚持认为；供养；
words.ex: He tries to maintain a healthy diet.
words.ex_cn: 他努力保持健康的饮食。
words.en: To keep something in existence or continue to provide support for it, especially over a period of time.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: He obtained a new job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周获得了一份新工作。
words.en: If you obtain something, you get it or achieve it.

words.ex: This forest has many different species of birds.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有多种不同的鸟类物种。
words.en: A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

words.ex: The creature lived in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个生物生活在森林里。
words.en: A creature is a living thing, especially an animal.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful creation of the artist.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是艺术家的一个美丽作品。
words.en: The act or process of bringing something into existence.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: The potter shaped the clay into a bowl.
words.ex_cn: 陶匠把黏土塑造成一个碗。
words.en: Clay is a type of fine-grained natural soil material that contains hydrous aluminium phyllosilicates (clay minerals) that develops plasticity when wet.

words.tr:
adj. 人的；人类的；
n. 人；人类；
words.ex: Human emotions are complex and powerful.
words.ex_cn: 人的情感复杂而强大。
words.en: A human is a member of the species Homo sapiens, distinguished from other animals by superior mental development, power of articulate speech, and upright stance.

words.tr: adj. 卑微的；谦逊的；虚心的；
words.ex: He lived in a humble house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他住在河边一座简陋的房子里。
words.en: If you describe someone as humble, you mean that they do not think they are better or more important than other people.

words.tr: n. 烟（西班牙语，意为烟雾）
words.ex: The fire produced a lot of humo.
words.ex_cn: 火灾产生了很多烟。
words.en: The quality of being amusing or comic, especially as expressed in literature or speech.

words.ex: The soil is moist after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后土壤是潮湿的。
words.en: Slightly wet; damp or humid.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.tr:
n. 寒冷；寒意；
v. 变冷；使冰冷；
words.ex: The chill of the morning made me wear a jacket.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的寒冷让我穿上了夹克。
words.en: A chill is a feeling of coldness, often accompanied by shivering. It can also refer to a feeling of fear or anxiety. As a verb, to chill means to make something cold, or to relax and take it easy.

words.ex: The ground is damp after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后地面是潮湿的。
words.en: Something that is damp is slightly wet, often in a way that is unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 损害；破损；
v. 损害；破坏；
words.ex: The storm caused serious damage to the house.
words.ex_cn: 风暴对房屋造成了严重损害。
words.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to something which makes it less attractive, useful, or valuable.

words.ex: They live in a small cottage near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小村舍里。
words.en: A cottage is a small house, usually in the countryside.

words.ex: They stayed in a small lodge near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小屋里。
words.en: A lodge is a small house in the country, especially one that is used by people on holiday or by people taking part in a sport such as skiing or hunting. As a verb, to lodge means to stay somewhere, especially temporarily, or to formally submit something, such as a complaint or an application.

words.tr:
n. 个人；
adj. 个别的；单独的；
words.ex: Each individual has the right to speak freely.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有权自由发言。
words.en: An individual is a person considered separately from their society or community. As an adjective, it describes something that is single, separate, or unique to a person or thing.

words.ex: She will divide the cake into two parts.
words.ex_cn: 她将把蛋糕分成两部分。
words.en: If you divide something, you separate it into two or more parts.

words.ex: This is my personal notebook.
words.ex_cn: 这是我的个人笔记本。
words.en: Relating to or belonging to a particular person rather than to a group or an organization.

words.ex: He keeps his diary private.
words.ex_cn: 他把日记保密。
words.en: If something is private, it is for the use of one person or group, rather than for the general public.

words.ex: The survey asks about your gender.
words.ex_cn: 这个调查询问你的性别。
words.en: Gender is the state of being male or female, especially when considered with reference to social and cultural differences, not just biological ones.

words.tr:
adj. 男性的；雄性的；
n. 男性；雄性；
words.ex: The male bird has bright red feathers.
words.ex_cn: 这只雄鸟有鲜艳的红色羽毛。
words.en: A male is a person or animal that belongs to the sex that cannot have babies. In humans, males are usually considered to be boys or men.

words.tr:
adj. 女性的；雌性的；
n. 雌性；女性；
words.ex: The female teacher is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 这位女老师非常和蔼。
words.en: A female is a person or animal that belongs to the sex that can have babies or produce eggs.

words.ex: The main reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The most important part or aspect of something.

words.ex: The temperature remains high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天温度保持很高。
words.en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；
n. 大调；主修课；
words.ex: Math is a major subject in school.
words.ex_cn: 数学是学校里的主要科目。
words.en: A major is a student's principal field of study or specialization in college or university.

words.ex: Pop music is part of the mainstream.
words.ex_cn: 流行音乐是主流的一部分。
words.en: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional.

words.ex: The stream flows quietly through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 小溪静静地流过森林。
words.en: A stream is a small, narrow river. It can also refer to a continuous flow of liquid, air, or gas, or a continuous flow of data or information.

words.ex: The boat travels through the canal.
words.ex_cn: 船通过运河航行。
